*Part of the [smallm](https://github.com/zekai128/smallm) series — building a transformer training library from scratch in C++/CUDA.*

## The three-matrix design

Raw token embeddings are a poor substrate for attention. If you directly computed $x_i \cdot x_j$ as the attention score, every token's ability to *query* and its ability to *be queried* would be coupled — the same vector serving both roles.

The solution is three learned projections:

$$\text{Attn}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_{\text{head}}}}\right) V$$

where $Q = XW_Q$, $K = XW_K$, $V = XW_V$.

## The scaling problem

The dot products $QK^T$ have variance proportional to $d_{\text{head}}$. Without scaling, a large $d_{\text{head}}$ pushes the softmax inputs into saturation — the exponentials collapse and all probability mass lands on one token.

Dividing by $\sqrt{d_{\text{head}}}$ normalizes variance back to ~1:

```cpp
float d_head = (float)(d_model / n_heads);
Tensor* attn_scaled = scale(attn_weights, 1.0f / sqrtf(d_head));
```

## Multi-head attention: shape algebra

After the QKV projections we get `[B*T, d_model]`. We reshape and permute to put the head dimension first, so cuBLAS treats heads as the batch dimension:

```
[B*T, d_model]  →reshape→  [B, T, H, d_head]  →permute(0,2,1,3)→  [B, H, T, d_head]
```

Then `matmul(Q, K)` gives `[B, H, T, T]` — one attention matrix per head per batch item.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Why not use 3D weight tensors and broadcasting?

The naive approach is $W_Q$ of shape `[1, d_model, d_model]` and broadcasting over the batch dim. The problem is cuBLAS `GemmStridedBatched` requires a fixed stride — it can't represent "same weight for all batches."

We instead fold: `[B, T, d_model] → [B*T, d_model]` before projecting. This is a 2D matmul and costs nothing since reshape is a zero-copy view operation.
:::

## The causal mask

A decoder must never attend to future tokens. We fill upper-triangle positions with $-10^9$ before softmax:

```cpp
// mask[i,j] = 1.0 where j > i (future tokens)
Tensor* masked = masked_fill(attn_scaled, causal_mask, -1e9f);
Tensor* attn_probs = softmax(masked);
```

After masking, future positions have softmax weight ~0. The model doesn't *learn* to ignore the future — the architecture makes it structurally impossible.

::: {.callout-warning}
Our `masked_fill` kernel uses the same flat index for mask and input — no broadcasting. The mask must be exactly `[B, n_heads, T, T]`.
:::
